name: Apple
headline: What the iPhone rebound means for Apple’s cash engine
summary: FY2026 cash generation improved sharply. The diligence question is how much of that improvement can survive a slower upgrade cycle.
thesis: The integrated hardware, software, and services ecosystem supports recurring engagement and pricing power. A sustainable underwriting case still depends on iPhone mix and Services margin.
counterargument: The FY2026 comparison benefited from strong Pro demand and a working-capital swing. Both can normalize while platform rules and manufacturing costs move against margins.
watch: iPhone mix and Greater China sales
Services gross margin and distribution terms
Inventory, payables and cash capital expenditure

claims.title: The upgrade cycle carried much of the growth
claims.detail: iPhone net sales rose from $209.6B to $254.1B, accounting for about 71% of the increase in consolidated net sales. The filing attributes iPhone growth primarily to Pro models.
claims.section: FY2026 10-K · Item 7 · Products and Services Performance

claims.title: Cash conversion improved faster than operating profit
claims.detail: Operating cash flow rose from $111.5B to $145.1B. Payables and other liabilities contributed positively, while inventory absorbed cash. The cash-flow uplift should be reconciled before extrapolation.
claims.section: FY2026 10-K · Item 8 · Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows

claims.title: Services adds a second source of profit
claims.detail: Services reached $123.3B of net sales. The filing cites advertising and cloud services as the principal drivers of growth. Underwrite the durability of this mix separately from hardware replacement.

basis: Audited fiscal years. Cash capital expenditure is payments for property, plant and equipment. FY2026 ended September 26.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.detail: Premium device mix holds and Services margin remains resilient.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.detail: Upgrade growth moderates and Services offsets part of the slower hardware cycle.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.detail: Weak device demand and changes to platform terms squeeze revenue and margin.

gate: Reconcile normalized working capital and run a combined iPhone mix and Services margin stress.
financing: No control transaction is assumed. Evaluate capacity after shareholder distributions, manufacturing commitments and a normalized cash conversion bridge.
governance: Review App Store litigation and regulatory remedies, supplier concentration, succession and privacy controls. Quantify distribution economics under alternative app terms.

name: Microsoft
headline: Microsoft’s cloud growth is running ahead of its cash conversion
summary: FY2026 revenue and operating cash flow rose. Cash spending on property and equipment climbed faster, so the economics depend on what the new capacity earns.
thesis: Azure and Microsoft 365 give Microsoft established distribution for AI. The underwriting case requires incremental capacity to generate durable cash returns after reinvestment.
counterargument: Customer ramp timing, pricing pressure and large partner exposures can leave Microsoft funding capacity ahead of realized demand.
watch: Cash additions to property and equipment and finance leases
Azure utilization, commercial backlog and margins

claims.title: Cash investment outpaced cash from operations
claims.detail: Operating cash flow rose from $136.2B to $182.9B. Cash additions to property and equipment rose from $64.6B to $115.9B, leaving $67.0B after cash capex versus $71.6B a year earlier.
claims.section: FY2026 10-K · Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows

claims.title: Cloud remains the primary growth engine
claims.detail: Microsoft Cloud revenue rose from $168.9B to $214.4B. Reported operating income rose from $128.5B to $155.2B.

claims.title: OpenAI exposure matters on both sides of the relationship
claims.detail: Microsoft disclosed $24.1B of FY2026 commercial revenue from arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue sharing, and a $6.0B receivable at year-end. Assess collection risk independently of the investment position.

basis: Audited fiscal years ended June 30. D&A historical proxy is the cash flow line “Depreciation, amortization, and other.” Cash capex excludes noncash lease additions.

timeline.title: Microsoft and OpenAI amend their agreement

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.detail: Azure and Microsoft 365 monetization absorb capacity quickly and free cash flow expands.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.detail: Cloud grows, but reinvestment limits near-term cash conversion.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.detail: Capacity commitments stay high as demand slows or partner collections weaken.

gate: Reconcile cash capex to lease-adjusted capacity commitments and test cloud utilization and OpenAI collections under a downside case.
financing: No sponsor buyout is assumed. Review the maturity ladder, lease obligations and cash investment alongside recurring enterprise cash generation.
governance: Review cloud and AI competition, data handling and incident controls. Monitor partner contract changes and related-party accounting.

name: Alphabet
headline: Can Google fund the AI buildout without weakening Search economics?
summary: Alphabet enters the AI transition with a strong advertising cash engine. The research question is whether new revenue keeps up with infrastructure spending and changes to distribution.
thesis: Search and YouTube provide distribution and cash generation. Cloud and Gemini create monetization paths, but underwriting requires evidence that AI answers and cloud demand earn back incremental capacity costs.
counterargument: Higher query volume can coexist with lower advertising value per query, and cloud growth can mask rising depreciation, power and third-party capacity costs.
watch: Search ad monetization and traffic acquisition costs
Cash capex, depreciation and Cloud operating margin
Implementation of U.S. search distribution remedies

claims.title: Cloud expanded from a smaller base
claims.detail: Google Cloud revenue rose from $43.2B in 2024 to $58.7B in 2025. Google Services still represented the majority of consolidated sales, so Search monetization remains central.

claims.title: Infrastructure spending accelerated
claims.detail: Cash capex rose from $52.5B to $91.4B in 2025. On its October 2026 earnings call, management kept its 2026 cash capex outlook at $195B–$205B and expected another significant increase in 2027.

claims.title: Search remedies affect distribution economics
claims.detail: The DOJ’s case docket records the final judgment and implementation filings. Model changes in default distribution and syndication terms separately from changes in user demand.
claims.section: US Department of Justice · Search case docket

basis: Audited calendar-year financials through 2025. Later Q3 2026 disclosure is separate. Historical depreciation is property and equipment depreciation only.

timeline.title: Q3 2026 results and capital expenditure outlook

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.detail: AI queries monetize without eroding Search contribution, and Cloud absorbs capacity at attractive margins.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.detail: Search monetization and Cloud growth partly offset a sustained reinvestment cycle.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.detail: Lower yield per query and adverse distribution changes coincide with elevated capital intensity.

gate: Stress Search revenue per query and traffic acquisition costs together with management’s capital expenditure outlook.
financing: No control transaction is assumed. Evaluate liquidity after infrastructure commitments and shareholder returns. A full equity bridge would need dated securities, debt and lease balances.
governance: Review the search and ad-tech dockets separately. Assess dual-class voting, data-use obligations, model security and jurisdiction-specific tax exposures.

name: Anthropic
headline: Anthropic’s prospectus puts a number on the cost of scaling Claude
summary: The amended S-1 provides financial visibility that funding headlines cannot. It also reveals long-dated infrastructure obligations that could constrain cash generation.
thesis: Claude’s rapid adoption has improved operating leverage, but the investment case depends on revenue durability, compute utilization and financing capacity against contracted commitments.
counterargument: Accelerating sales and positive nine-month operating cash flow may mask payment timing, preferred-stock economics and long-dated commitments.
watch: Quarterly revenue and operating results by period
Compute purchase and lease commitments by due date
Final offer price, fully diluted shares and voting rights

claims.title: Quarterly revenue grew rapidly, with an operating loss
claims.detail: Q3 2026 revenue was $16.956B against $1.382B a year earlier. The latest quarter still had a $567M operating loss. The quarterly figures in the prospectus are unaudited.
claims.section: November 2 S-1/A · Quarterly Results of Operations

claims.title: Net loss and cash generation tell different stories
claims.detail: Nine-month 2026 operating loss was $1.260B and operating cash flow was positive $6.569B. The $104.039B net loss included a $94.324B change in fair value of financing instruments.
claims.section: November 2 S-1/A · Summary Financial Data and Cash Flows

claims.title: Commitments extend well beyond the near term
claims.detail: The prospectus discloses about $895.4B of aggregate committed spend, mostly compute and infrastructure, including about $69.8B due in the next 12 months. The aggregate spans multiple years and is not booked debt.

basis: Audited annual statements from the S-1/A, with unaudited interim figures shown separately. No final offer price or traded return series is used.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.detail: Paid usage and retention absorb reserved compute while unit delivery cost falls.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.detail: Claude grows quickly, with continuing cash needs and uneven operating profitability.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.detail: Pricing, distribution or utilization disappoints while multi-year spending remains committed.

gate: Verify final offering terms and build a quarterly commitments, liquidity and dilution bridge before pricing equity.
financing: Compare spending by contractual due date with available liquidity and committed financing. Confirm cancellation and performance clauses. Preferred shares, convertible notes and lease commitments require separate treatment.
governance: Review proposed voting control, public benefit duties, related-party arrangements and model safety governance. Inspect litigation and the cash timing of settlements.

name: OpenAI
headline: OpenAI’s funding scale makes cash visibility more important
summary: ChatGPT distribution, enterprise products and the API create several revenue channels. Public funding announcements leave key questions about profitability, liquidity and the cost of serving demand.
thesis: A broad distribution base creates room for subscription, enterprise and API monetization. The underwriting case depends on contribution margin after compute, recurring customer spend and funding against contractual capacity.
counterargument: High usage and committed capital can coexist with negative cash flow, declining unit pricing, and high dependence on a small number of infrastructure partners.
watch: Audited consolidated accounts and cash flow
Compute economics and customer cohort retention
Signed funding terms, cap table and partner obligations

claims.title: Funding headlines measure capital terms
claims.detail: OpenAI announced $122B in committed capital at an $852B post-money valuation on March 31, 2026. This is a dated financing reference. It does not establish unrestricted cash, current fair value or an enterprise value.

claims.title: Infrastructure access brings obligations
claims.detail: Amazon’s September 10-Q records a $50B preferred investment and describes commercial arrangements with OpenAI. OpenAI’s announcement described a multi-year AWS agreement expansion. Analyze the investment and the customer commitment separately.

claims.title: The nonprofit controls the operating company
claims.detail: OpenAI states that its Foundation controls OpenAI Group PBC through special voting and governance rights. Investment rights and board control need separate underwriting.

basis: No audited standalone income statement, balance sheet or cash-flow series was verified in the public sources reviewed. Announced commitments are tracked separately from company financials.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.detail: Enterprise adoption compounds and infrastructure cost per paid task falls.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.detail: Monetization expands while capacity growth keeps funding needs material.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.detail: Competition compresses API prices and compute commitments outlast demand growth.

risk: Unverified cash runway and contract exposure
gate: Obtain audited standalone statements, signed compute commitments, a fully diluted cap table and a financing-to-cash reconciliation.
financing: Verify closing conditions and cash receipts separately from commitments. Reconcile priority rights and convertibles, then model contracted payments by quarter. No sponsor deal is assumed.
governance: Review nonprofit board rights, PBC purpose, related-party terms, copyright and privacy litigation, and independent safety and incident reporting.
